Definition: from G4754; military service, i.e. (figuratively) the apostolic career (as one of hardship and danger):--warfare.
BiblicalUsage: Warfare is the campaign itself, and Paul uses it for the ministry. Timothy is to war a good warfare by the prophecies that went before on him, and the weapons of our warfare are not carnal, but mighty through God to the pulling down of strong holds.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the warfare is real and the weapons are not: prayer and truth pull down what swords cannot.
